# Codex Cryptica

> A private, local-first campaign manager for lore keepers who value privacy, speed, visual organisation, and AI-assisted worldbuilding.

## Core Product

- [Codex Cryptica](https://codexcryptica.com/): The primary entry point. A free, local-first RPG campaign manager and worldbuilding tool.
- [Full User Guide & Features](https://codexcryptica.com/llms-full.txt): Complete AI-readable feature and help documentation.

## Key Features

- Knowledge Graph: Visualise entities and relationships as an interactive node-link diagram.
- AI Oracle: Context-aware lore assistant powered by Google Gemini — optional, vault-aware.
- Local-First Storage: Vault data is stored in the browser using OPFS. No cloud account required.
- Map & VTT Mode: Use maps, pins, fog of war, tokens, initiative, and tactical play.
- Spatial Canvas: Build conspiracy boards, quest flows, faction webs, and relationship maps.
- Markdown Ownership: All vault files are plain Markdown with YAML frontmatter — no lock-in.
- Offline Support: The wiki, graph, timeline, and canvas work fully without internet access.

## Privacy & AI Policy

Codex Cryptica is local-first: vault data is stored locally by default and does not require a cloud account. AI features are optional. When AI features are used, only the selected or retrieved context needed for that request is sent to the configured AI provider. Read the full responsible AI principles at https://codexcryptica.com/responsible-ai-worldbuilding.

## Comparisons

- [Codex Cryptica vs World Anvil](https://codexcryptica.com/vs/world-anvil): Local-first privacy vs cloud-hosted worldbuilding platform.
- [Codex Cryptica vs Obsidian](https://codexcryptica.com/vs/obsidian): Lore-native graph and entity structure vs general-purpose notes.
- [Codex Cryptica vs LegendKeeper](https://codexcryptica.com/vs/legendkeeper): Visual worldbuilding, maps, AI assistance, and vault control.
- [Codex Cryptica vs Kanka](https://codexcryptica.com/vs/kanka-alternative): Local-first offline use vs cloud-based campaign wiki.

## Live In-Browser Generators

The pages above are informational landing pages; these are the canonical, no-login-required tools that actually generate and let you save a draft into a vault. The `/tools/*` pages above link into these for the interactive experience.

- [Generators Hub](https://codexcryptica.com/generators): Directory of every live in-browser RPG generator, grouped by genre.
- [RPG NPC Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/npc): Generate a full NPC — name, ancestry, role, secret, faction tie, and GM hook — across any genre, no account required.
- [Faction Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/faction): Generate a faction with agenda, leadership, resources, rivals, and hooks.
- [Settlement Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/settlement): Generate a town, city, or outpost with population, industry, threats, and points of interest.
- [Magic Item Generator](https://codexcryptica.com/generators/magic-item): Generate a magic item with properties, history, and drawbacks.

## Answer Pages

Concise, self-contained reference answers to real RPG and worldbuilding questions. Each page answers the question directly before any product material.

- [Answers Hub](https://codexcryptica.com/answers): Index of every published answer page.
- [What is a point crawl?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/what-is-a-point-crawl): Mapping an adventure as named locations joined by explicit routes, rather than a hex grid.
- [How do you organise RPG campaign notes?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-organise-rpg-campaign-notes): Durable entity pages, dated session logs, and disposable prep — plus the post-session pass that keeps them true.
- [How do you create a fantasy faction?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-create-a-fantasy-faction): Six questions — goal, obstacle, recruits, limits, assets, next move — that make a faction act on its own.
- [How do you organise NPC relationships?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-organise-npc-relationships): Store relationships as directed, named links with a reason and a visibility, not as ally lists.
- [What makes a good random encounter?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/what-makes-a-good-random-encounter): A situation already in progress, with a reason to be there and an option that is not combat.
- [How do you create a pantheon?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-create-a-pantheon): Build entanglements between gods before assigning domains; five structural moves that generate play.
- [How do you design RPG puzzles that do not stall the game?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-design-rpg-puzzles-that-do-not-stall-the-game): More than one way through, and failure that costs something other than time.
- [What should an RPG settlement contain?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/what-should-an-rpg-settlement-contain): A reason to exist, three or four enterable places, three people who want things, and one unsolved problem.
- [How do you create a believable fictional religion?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-create-a-believable-fictional-religion): Write the practice before the doctrine: one rite, one prohibition, who funds it, and what adherents dispute.
- [How do you run a conspiracy campaign?](https://codexcryptica.com/answers/how-do-you-run-a-conspiracy-campaign): Decide the truth in full before session one, then design how it leaks; every conclusion needs three routes.
